description: Whether cavity/antenna-enhanced inverse Faraday effect bias survives the scale-down from extended films to recording media. The question 'does it scale to grain size' is itself welded: recording bits are grain CLUSTERS (~10-100 grains, ~50-90 nm), and the amplifier already reaches that scale. What actually does not scale as one thing: intensity (fine), geometry (fine), material response (the fork), and antenna durability (the wall the industry already paid once).

components.name: IFE per-volume response
components.law: inverse Faraday effect magnetization is intensive - per unit volume, proportional to local intensity; it does not dilute with grain size. Weak in FePt (polar Kerr ~0.87%), adequate in Co/Pt-class (susceptibility 2.1e-11 A m V^-2 used in models)

components.name: antenna/cavity intensity enhancement
components.law: gold nanodisks give ~30x intensity enhancement with ~90 nm hot spots over 6 nm Co/Pt (modeled); microcavities give giant IFE peaks at band edge but with high Q (long dwell time)

components.name: antenna durability at recording duty cycle
components.law: gold NFTs run >300 C at ~150 TW/m^2; gold becomes malleable near 400 K and surface-diffuses above ~150 C over ambient; cyclic fatigue and geometry drift move the hot spot. HAMR took ~20 years because the antenna cooked itself; it now ships at PMR-parity reliability (5-year warranty, 2.5M-hour MTBF)

components.name: hot-spot confinement vs bit geometry
components.law: recording bits are grain clusters (~50-90 nm for current HAMR tracks); 90 nm hot spots already match. 'Grain-size addressing' is not the target - bit-cluster addressing is, and it is already industrial in the thermal term (HAMR delivers <30 nm thermal spots to granular FePt)

components.name: material-class anisotropy fork
components.law: the IFE field needed scales with anisotropy: modeled >90% switching probability on Co/Pt at H_z > 0.3 T with T_e < 2000 K; FePt needs ~10 T for ~0.6 ps (Ellis 2016). The IFE-friendly class is Co/Pt; the retention-strong class is FePt

components.name: retention barrier at grain scale (unmeasured)
components.law: whether Co/Pt-class multilayers hold adequate energy barriers (Delta ~ 40-60 for 10-year retention) at ~10 nm grains is claimed (UCSD paper: 'high thermal stability even at nanometer-scale bit volumes') but the energy barrier per bit was never measured inside any frame - the S2 finding from the thickness-ceiling case returns at this level

rejected.ruled_out_by: Q-smearing: cavity enhancement requires high Q (long dwell time), which stretches picosecond steering pulses; cavity modes are extended-film phenomena (lambda^3 mode volume). The fast, confined route is necessarily plasmonic, not cavity

rejected.option: antenna-free single-pulse IFE switching of FePt
rejected.ruled_out_by: damage threshold: unenhanced IFE needs ~10 T effective fields; the required fluence exceeds the medium damage threshold
bit geometry: recording bits are grain clusters; the amplifier must reach the cluster (it does), not the isolated grain (it need not)

budget_terms: antenna lifetime (thermal budget at recording duty cycle)
IFE field to anisotropy-field ratio (0.3 T Co/Pt vs ~10 T FePt)

diagnostic.note: both walls are located and documented: the material fork is modeled (Co/Pt 0.3 T vs FePt 10 T) and the durability wall is industrial history (HAMR's 20-year NFT delay, now shipping). Neither is a law - one is a material-class conditional, the other a paid-once engineering cost

source_class: collected - published models and industry data (Cheng et al. ACS Photonics 2023 plasmon-enhanced AOS model; Ellis et al. 2016 IFE thresholds; Seagate/Evatec HAMR head materials paper; Trinh 2020 NFT failure study; Seagate Mozaic reliability announcements)
open: whether antenna intensity enhancement (~30x modeled, 100x+ possible) brings FePt's ~10 T IFE requirement down to deliverable sub-damage fluence - unmodeled and untested; this is the load-bearing open experiment

whether Co/Pt-class retention at grain scale is real - the energy barrier per bit was never measured inside any frame in this chain (the S2 recursion: the same unmeasured quantity reappears at every level of the descent)
whether the dual-pulse fs-demagnetize + ps-steer scheme survives the lossy plasmonic environment - the antenna absorbs on the ps timescale too, feeding the durability term

CrPt-class materials show coherent nonthermal IFE switching within a few hundred fs - the material-class fork may dissolve entirely with the right magnetooptical response, dissolving this constraint the way the thickness ceiling dissolved
